widgets_values:
Exercise: object instance detection using a homography

Given a reference image of a planar object (Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night') and a cluttered scene (a wall with three public-domain paintings hung at an angle), locate the object and draw its outline. The 'Feature Match + RANSAC Homography' subgraph detects SIFT features (scale/rotation robust - essential here, the poster appears far smaller and tilted on the wall), filters the reference keypoints, matches them, and estimates the reference->scene homography with RANSAC. The four corners of the reference ('Reference corners') are projected into the scene with cv2.perspectiveTransform and connected with 'Draw Polygon'. Failure-tolerant: if the object is absent the homography node reports found=false and a 'Basic data handling' if/else routes the plain scene to the preview (its lazy inputs bypass the drawing branch entirely).

Why SIFT + a keypoint filter (open the subgraph): a high-res reference yields thousands of TINY (size ~2px) keypoints. The same painting is smaller and tilted on the wall, so those fine-scale features have no counterpart there - they only add ambiguous matches and burn the descriptor budget. 'Filter Keypoints' (min_size) drops them: ~8000 reference keypoints collapse to ~470 large, structurally meaningful ones, yet the RANSAC inlier count barely changes. A raw 'max_features' count cannot express 'keep the reliable features' - it is the wrong, misleading knob.

Debug previews: keypoints drawn on BOTH images (rich circles sized by scale - compare the filtered reference to the busy scene), the RANSAC inlier matches, and the inlier count (a low count, < ~10, means a likely false positive). Note the scene needs a high max_features (20000): 2000 features spread over a 1500px-wide wall starve the small target and the match fails. The pipeline runs on raw ndarrays; only previews convert back to tensors.

Approach 2 (the parallel branch in the lower band, blue dashed outline): instead of filtering, DOWNSCALE the reference so its features are born at the scene's scale - a different, simpler way to handle the same small-descriptor problem. See its note.

FAILURE IS VISIBLE, NOT SILENT: both lanes fall back to the PLAIN scene when no homography is found, which used to make a failure look exactly like a success. 'found' is still the real answer - branch on it, and read it off the inlier-count previews - but the false branch now also stamps NOT FOUND onto its own copy of the image, so the PICTURE cannot be misread either. That stamp belongs HERE, in the workflow: a node or a subgraph must never bake a message into the data it returns.

nodes.title: [Feature Match + RANSAC Homography] Reference -> Scene Homography
if found: outlined scene, else: plain scene
Preview as Text: Inspect (inlier count - low = false positive)
Detect Features (resized ref, SIFT, no filter)
if found: outlined scene, else: plain scene
Preview as Text: Inspect (resize-branch inlier count)

widgets_values:
Approach 2: handle small descriptors by RESIZING the reference instead of filtering keypoints.

The reference is downscaled to 25% (cv2.resize, INTER_AREA) - roughly the size the poster occupies on the wall. SIFT then computes descriptors at scales that actually EXIST in the scene, so no keypoint filtering is needed (Detect Features here has no Filter Keypoints after it). About 350 keypoints give ~52 RANSAC inliers - a far higher inlier RATIO than the full-res branch (52/350 vs ~32/2000), because every feature is born at a matchable scale.

Trade-off vs Approach 1 (Filter Keypoints): resizing is simpler and gives cleaner matches when you know the object's approximate on-scene size, but it bakes in one scale; filtering keeps the full-res descriptors and lets RANSAC pick. The projected outline (GREEN) lands on the same poster as the red one. Corners come from the RESIZED reference, so perspectiveTransform maps resized-ref -> scene correctly.
